29 October 2026, Brisbane. Root's next construction after the exact clock
frontier. This note combines positive semigroup geometry with a quantitative
microscopic path comparison. Complete positivity here is the classical
nonnegative Gram cone, not quantum complete positivity.

## 1. Scope and objects

Q is a finite irreducible row CTMC generator, pi>0 its stationary law.
Every microscopic state is even under the stipulated physical time
reversal. Let sigma be its usual stationary Markov entropy rate, in
nats per time. The claim is about this model class; a different odd-state
reversal or a non-Markov microscopic model is not ruled out by it.

A symmetric matrix C is completely positive (CP) if C=B B^T for an
entrywise nonnegative rectangular B. A symmetric H is copositive if
x^T H x>=0 for every x>=0. These cones are dual. Put

    h_minus=max(0,-min_ij H_ij).

A negative pairing with any nonnegative C requires h_minus>0.
All witness bounds below may use h_minus; max|H_ij| is a valid weaker
scale. No general efficient copositivity oracle is assumed.

For stationary lag data let E_xa be deterministic visible labels or a
nonnegative emission kernel with sum_a E_xa=1. The uncentered two-time
joint matrix is

    C(t)=E^T diag(pi) exp(tQ) E.

For stochastic emissions the two sample draws are conditionally independent
given the hidden path; correlated sensor memory is not described by E.
Use t>0 operationally. At t=0 this formula for stochastic E describes
two replicated emissions, not a single variable paired with itself.
Use C_sym=(C+C^T)/2. Arbitrary unnormalized nonnegative features need an
extra scale bound; the probability-normalized statements do not apply
unchanged to them.

# What the native entropy assay acquired

29 October 2026, Brisbane.

## Declared consequence and source access

The target is a lower bound on stationary Markov entropy production of
EVERY compatible finite CTMC with all states even under the specified
reversal. Neither the hidden generator nor its state count is identified.

The native interface supplies five individually resettable microscopic
ports, equal calibrated stationary departure flux weights, native port
holding rate32/15, independent repetitions, return endpoints, an explicit
direct-jump marker, and duration intervals of width2^-20. These are
supplied source/instrument conditions. They are not learned by the assay.

The per-departure entropy certificate uses a bounded endpoint score and
requires no tail envelope or hidden rate ceiling. Conversion to a rate
per native time additionally uses the supplied conditional bound
P(tau>t)<=exp(-t/2) on interior duration. It bounds the unresolved tail
after truncation at24. Native initial holds are included; their mean15/32
